newsitem.title: USA: TransTexas North Dakota well producing.
newsitem.headline: TransTexas North Dakota well producing.

text.p: TransTexas Gas Corp said Tuesday production from its Heart River No. 1 discovery well, located in Dickinson, N.D., has confirmed the discovery of a productive oil field.

The well is flowing light, 41 degree gravity, sweet crude at a sustained rate of 4,500 barrels per day from the Lodgepole formation, through a 44/64-inch choke with flowing tubing pressure of 575 pounds per square inch.

As a result of the additional production available with its new pipeline connection with Koch in North Dakota and incremental Bob West North natural gas production in Texas, TransTexas said, its daily gross production capacity has increased 53 percent from August 1 to some 800 million cubic feet of natural gas equivalent.
TransTexas had previously reported the well encountered 308 feet of carbonate Lodgepole reef, containing an oil column of about 140 feet.
The company said it expects to conduct an optimized flow-test within the next week after adding additional perforations in the productive zones.

"Based upon the production from the Heart River No. 1, drilling results of a first delineation well and 3-D seismic information, we estimate that this field may ultimately prove to contain as much as 10-12 million barrels of oil," the company said.
"This represents an excellent return on our $40 million in capital expenditures," it pointed out.
The company said it is drilling an offsetting delineation well, the Dinsdale No. 2-4, that it believes has penetrated the reef and expects to conclude and log within the week.
A third well, the Dinsdale No. 1-3 is scheduled to start drilling from the same pad in early December and is expected to further expand this new field.
The field is located along trend from the large Conoco/Duncan Eland field, to the south-west and DuPont Co's Conoco Dickinson field to the north-west.

TransTexas will be the operator, with an average working interest of about 80 percent, it said. Privately-held, unaffiliated, third-party companies, with mineral interests in the Williston Basin of North Dakota, hold the balance of 20 percent working interest.
